title: Morena Distances Itself from Rocha Moya. Opposition Revives the “Narco-Party” Narrative.
author: Redacción / SinEmbargo
content:
_This article by[Redacción /
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/redaccion/) originally appeared
in the [August 21, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4858174/regreso-de-rocha-moya-da-vuelo-
a-la-oposicion-y-alimenta-narrativa-de-narcopartido), one of Mexico’s leading
independent digital news outlets._

**Mexico City, August 21 (SinEmbargo).—** Morena announced that it had no
knowledge that Rubén Rocha Moya would return this Friday to his post as
Governor of Sinaloa, and so it distanced itself from this strictly personal
decision.

> This leadership had no prior knowledge of the governor’s personal decision.
> Therefore, Morena distances itself from this decision.
>
> Morena

It also recalled that the governor’s leave came after the accusations from the
United States Department of Justice, which accuse Rocha of colluding with the
Sinaloa Cartel, and it stressed that Mexico’s Attorney General’s Office and
other Mexican authorities are maintaining investigations on the matter.

**“At Morena we will be respectful of the rule of law, of due process, as well
as of the outcome of the investigations by the Attorney General’s Office, and
we will continue acting with responsibility, prioritizing the interest of the
citizenry and maintaining as fundamental principles transparency,
accountability and unrestricted respect for institutions,”** it asserted.

> [Post by @PartidoMorenaMx on
> X](https://twitter.com/PartidoMorenaMx/status/2090901647127970298)

Previously, the Secretariat of Governance issued a communiqué in which it
emphasized that Rocha Moya’s return to the governorship was a decision of a
personal nature, and it added that the Attorney General’s Office has open
investigation files related to the 10 people named by the U.S. Department of
Justice, among them the Sinaloa governor.

**“The Secretariat of Governance reports that Dr. Rubén Rocha Moya’s decision
to reincorporate into his functions as Governor of the state of Sinaloa
responds exclusively to a determination of a personal nature,”** the
representation of the Mexican Government stated.

Regarding the inquiry, it added that the Secretariat of Foreign Relations
(SRE) has repeatedly asked the U.S. to provide the corresponding evidence to
support the claims made, but that it is up to the Attorney General’s Office to
provide any additional information it deems pertinent.

This Friday, Rocha Moya announced that he will once again assume his post as
Governor of Sinaloa after remaining on leave for more than 112 days, and he
maintained that he is innocent. He also described the accusations against him
as false and **“with political and interventionist motivations of the national
and foreign far right.”**

For their part, various opposition figures criticized the Morena member’s
return to the governorship, among them Alejandro “Alito” Moreno, senator and
leader of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI); Jorge Álvarez Máynez,
leader of Movimiento Ciudadano (MC); and Guadalupe Acosta Naranjo, of Somos
México.

Through their social media, the opposition party leaders spread messages in
which they reiterated their accusations of Morena as a “narco-party.”

“Alito” Moreno, leader of the PRI, published a message on his X account,
formerly Twitter, in which he accused Rocha Moya of being a “narco-politician”
backed by Morena and questioned that the Morena member is once again assuming
his post as Governor of Sinaloa without having cleared up the accusations
against him for allegedly having ties to organized crime.

**“Rubén Rocha Moya and Morena are mocking the people of Sinaloa when they
claim that the Attorney General’s Office already proved he committed no crime.
This is further proof of how the Mexican State has turned the justice
institutions into tools to grant impunity to the country’s worst criminals and
to persecute, with all the power of the apparatus, those of us who dare to
criticize them,”** the message reads.

> [Post by @alitomorenoc on
> X](https://twitter.com/alitomorenoc/status/2090876519597879727)

The PRI member asserted that his party **“will not rest until it removes
Morena from Sinaloa”** and stated that the Morena member will again assume the
state’s governorship without the backing of the Sinaloa population.

Álvarez Máynez, leader of MC, joined the opposition’s criticism of Rocha
Moya’s return to the Government of Sinaloa with a message shared on his social
media, in which he stated that this will be a “day of national shame.”

**“It is a mockery of our country, the cynicism and impunity that this message
represents,”** the MC member posted, in a publication in which he cited the
Morena member’s announcement.

The recently created party Somos México, linked to businessman Claudio X.
González, published a communiqué in which it claimed that Rocha Moya’s return
to the governorship is a decision by President Claudia Sheinbaum and her
predecessor, Andrés Manuel López Obrador (AMLO), to protect Morena members
accused of allegedly having ties to drug trafficking.

Furthermore, the document underscores that the Morena member’s return to the
state’s governorship is an affront to the U.S. government and endangers the
country’s sovereignty.

**“Far from defending sovereignty, this decision places it in a position of
vulnerability by turning the Rocha case into an irresponsible provocation and
a confrontation with the United States, our main trading partner,”** the
communiqué says.

> [Post by @SomosMxMexico on
> X](https://twitter.com/SomosMxMexico/status/2090875250816749766)

For his part, the leader of Somos México, Guadalupe Acosta Naranjo, also
published a message in which he asserted that President Sheinbaum is part of
an impunity pact to protect Morena members accused of having ties to drug
trafficking.

**“The impunity pact, the protection of narco-terrorists, the cynicism and the
cowardice will pursue President Claudia Sheinbaum forever. All to protect
Andrés Manuel López Obrador, his accomplices and relatives, regardless of
putting our country and its citizens at risk,”** the message reads.
